newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday, May 20.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimo D'Alema said that considering the country's high rate of unemployment, affecting mostly young people in the south, it was not sustainable for the government to keep paying early retirement pensions. D'Alema said it should not be possible for workers to finish work at 50 (all).

* In an interview, hard left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said PDS stand on pensions' reforms was wrong and repeated pensions' cuts should be the last step in welfare state reforms and ought not to be discussed before 2008 (Corriere della Sera).

* Marcello Dell'Utri, a parliamentary deputy for centre-right opposition and a former business colleague of Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi, was ordered to stand trial on charges of mafia association (all).

* The foundation that controls Italy's largest savings bank Cariplo voted to open talks on merger with banking group Ambroveneto, an operation which could create the nation's largest banking group (all).
* Expectations of a cut in Italy's discount rate boosted the lira exchange rate and fixed income markets: the lira rose to 980.65 against the German mark while Btp futures rose over 131 (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
